channel.title: Blockheight
channel.description: Blockheight reports crypto news: Bitcoin and Ethereum, DeFi protocols, exchanges, stablecoins, regulation, security incidents and market structure.

item.title: Check the token before a cross-chain transfer
item.description: Check the token contract and destination network before bridging; matching tickers do not prove matching assets, and route support can change the outcome.

item.title: Bridge limits depend on route, liquidity and transfer design
item.description: Large crypto transfers can hit bridge caps, liquidity gaps or token mismatches; check the route’s limits and settlement steps before sending funds across chains.

item.title: Bridged tokens can arrive before you have gas to use them
item.description: If you reach a new chain without its gas token, bridged assets can stay in your wallet until you fund a fee or use a bridge that covers destination gas.

item.title: Browser network settings can hide wallet balances after recovery
item.description: A browser’s connection can block wallet data or RPC access, but it cannot change a recovery phrase; check the account, chain and network endpoint.

item.title: How to Fund an Escrow Payment From Your Crypto Wallet
item.description: Fund an escrow payment by matching the asset and network in the instructions, checking the deposit address, and sending only the stated amount and fee.

item.title: What Price Impact Warnings Mean in Cross-Chain Swaps
item.description: Price impact warnings estimate how a cross-chain swap moves available liquidity; learn how routes, slippage and fees affect the amount that arrives.

item.title: How to Turn LP Proceeds Into the Token You Need
item.description: LP proceeds become a usable token after you separate fees from principal, withdraw the position, and compare swap and bridge costs along the route.

item.title: Why a Cross-Chain Swap Can Stay Pending or Fail
item.description: A cross-chain swap can confirm on its source chain while the destination transfer is still pending; check both transactions before retrying or claiming a refund.

item.title: Wallet permits can replace a separate token approval
item.description: A permit can skip a separate token approval transaction, but the signature still sets who may spend tokens, how much they may spend and when it can be used.

item.title: Gas sponsorship removes one hurdle, not swap costs
item.description: Gas sponsorship can remove the need to hold a chain’s native token upfront, but cross-chain swaps still carry network, bridge and execution costs.

item.title: Liquidity bridges move tokens before source funds settle
item.description: Liquidity bridges deliver tokens by fronting destination funds, but custody shifts among contracts, liquidity providers and the keys that control withdrawals.

item.title: Visa Direct puts USDC prefunding into production with Inyo
item.description: Visa says Inyo Global is first to put Visa Direct USDC prefunding into commercial production, letting eligible businesses fund cross-border payouts near real time.

item.title: How to Confirm a Cross-Chain Treasury Transfer
item.description: A cross-chain treasury transfer is confirmed only when the source debit and destination credit match, the bridge route has settled and the receiving wallet is checked.

item.title: Revoking a token approval can interrupt recurring swaps
item.description: Revoking a token allowance can make the next scheduled swap fail, but it may not cancel the schedule; check the spender, balance and automation status.

item.title: How to Verify a Mantle Bridge Deposit Network
item.description: Verify a Mantle deposit by matching its source transaction, destination address and network in the explorers; a token ticker alone does not confirm the transfer.

item.title: How Integrators Schedule Cross-Chain Transfers Under Load
item.description: Integrators schedule cross-chain transfers by pricing routes, reserving liquidity and pacing submissions as congestion changes cost, delivery time and failure risk.

item.title: How Businesses Should Reconcile Cross-Chain Transfers
item.description: Reconcile a cross-chain transfer by matching source and destination records, accounting for fees and timing, and documenting exceptions before closing the books.

item.title: Paying a merchant from the wrong chain
item.description: When checkout names the wrong network, match the merchant’s chain first, then bridge or swap only after checking the asset, fees and final recipient.

item.title: Four Checks When a Crypto Withdrawal Review Delays Funding
item.description: A crypto withdrawal review can pause funding for identity, risk or network checks; these four steps help identify the hold, avoid duplicate requests and see what to do next.

item.title: BTC to native ETH requires a swap, not a bridge
item.description: BTC does not become native ETH through a bridge: swap it for ETH, then receive it on Ethereum mainnet; bridged BTC remains a separate token.
